note: Encodes section 11 of swing-knowledge-base.md. T = torso length (hip midpoint to shoulder midpoint at address). Seed values: tune against your own swings.

rules.name: Posture at address
rules.praise: Your posture at address is in a good range: {value} of forward bend from the hips.

rules.name: Knee flex at address
rules.praise: Athletic knee flex at address ({value}).

rules.name: Arm hang at address
rules.praise: Your arms hang naturally under your shoulders at address.

rules.name: Posture kept to the top
rules.praise: You kept your forward bend through the backswing.

rules.name: Head height in the backswing
rules.praise: Your head stayed at a steady height going back.

rules.name: Shoulder plane at the top
rules.praise: Your shoulders turned on a nicely tilted plane at the top.

rules.name: Trail knee flex kept at the top
Early extension
rules.praise: No early extension: your hips stayed back through impact.

rules.name: Posture at impact
rules.praise: You held your posture into impact.

rules.name: Trail heel at the finish
rules.praise: Trail heel up at the finish: your weight got through.

rules.name: Balanced finish
rules.praise: You held a still, balanced finish.

rules.name: Tilt at address
rules.praise: Good upper-body tilt away from the target at address ({value}).

rules.name: Sway
rules.praise: No sway: your hips turned without sliding away from the target.

rules.name: Hip shift at impact
rules.praise: Good shift onto your lead side by impact ({value} toward the target).

rules.name: Shoulder tilt at impact
rules.praise: Trail shoulder nicely lower than the lead at impact ({value}).

rules.name: Finish over the lead side
rules.praise: You finished with your weight over your lead side.

rules.name: Tempo
rules.praise: Your tempo is close to the 3:1 rhythm good players share ({value}).

rules.name: Head during the chip
rules.praise: Steady head through the chip.

rules.name: Short-game tempo
rules.praise: Smooth 2:1 short-game rhythm ({value}).

rules.name: Head during the putt
rules.praise: Very still head through the putt.

rules.name: Putting stroke length
rules.praise: Backstroke and through-stroke are well matched.

too_upright.name: Standing too upright
too_upright.seen: Your forward bend at address was {value}; for a {club} about {expected} works better.
too_upright.why: Standing tall makes it hard to turn on a tilted plane and usually leads to standing up further in the swing.

too_bent.name: Bent over too far
too_bent.seen: Your forward bend at address was {value}; for a {club} about {expected} is typical.
too_bent.why: Too much bend puts weight on the toes and makes it hard to keep your posture as you turn.

stiff_knees.name: Stiff legs at address
stiff_knees.seen: Your knees were almost straight at address ({value} of flex; {expected} is athletic).
stiff_knees.why: Locked knees make it hard to turn the hips and to stay balanced.

too_much_knee.name: Too much knee bend
too_much_knee.seen: You squatted into {value} of knee flex at address ({expected} is typical).
too_much_knee.why: Sitting down with little hip bend works in bunkers but makes full swings hard to repeat.

crowded.name: Hands crowded into the body
crowded.seen: Your hands sat {value} inside your shoulders at address.
crowded.why: Crowded arms have no room to swing past the body.

reaching.name: Reaching for the ball
reaching.seen: Your hands sat {value} out beyond your shoulders at address.
reaching.why: Reaching puts weight on the toes and encourages losing posture.

loss_of_posture.name: Losing your posture
loss_of_posture.seen: You lost {value} of forward bend from address.
loss_of_posture.why: Changing your setup angles moves the bottom of the swing and causes thin and topped shots.

head_rise.name: Head rising
head_rise.why: Rising up usually means you're standing out of your posture, which leads to thin contact.

head_drop.name: Head dropping
head_drop.why: A big drop moves the low point of the swing and can cause fat shots.

early_extension.name: Early extension
early_extension.seen: Your hips moved {value} toward the ball (keep it under {limit}).
early_extension.why: When the hips move toward the ball the arms get stuck behind you; the usual misses are a block right and a hook left.

flat_shoulders.name: Flat shoulder turn
flat_shoulders.seen: At the top your shoulders turned flatter than your posture ({value} of your address bend).
flat_shoulders.why: A level shoulder turn usually comes with standing up, which hurts contact.

over_the_top.name: Possible over-the-top move
over_the_top.seen: Starting down, your hands looked to move {value} out toward the ball compared with the way they went up. The app can't see the club, so treat this as a hint.
over_the_top.why: Throwing the hands out from the top is a common cause of slices and pulls.

heel_down.name: Trail heel stayed down
heel_down.seen: Your trail heel lifted only {value} at the finish.
heel_down.why: A flat trail foot at the finish usually means your weight didn't get onto your lead side.

unbalanced_finish.name: No balanced finish
unbalanced_finish.seen: The app didn't find a finish you held still.
unbalanced_finish.why: Holding a balanced finish shows the weight shift and rotation worked; falling back means they didn't.

stance_narrow.name: Stance narrow for this club
stance_narrow.seen: Your feet were {value} of shoulder width apart; about {expected} suits a {club}.
stance_narrow.why: Too narrow a stance costs stability, especially with longer clubs.

stance_wide.name: Stance wide for this club
stance_wide.seen: Your feet were {value} of shoulder width apart; about {expected} suits a {club}.
stance_wide.why: Too wide a stance restricts your hip turn.

tilt_too_little.name: Not enough tilt at address
tilt_too_little.seen: Your upper body tilted {value} away from the target; about {expected} suits a {club}.
tilt_too_little.why: Without some tilt away from the target the upper body tends to get ahead of the ball, and the driver can't catch it on the way up.

tilt_too_much.name: Too much tilt at address
tilt_too_much.seen: Your upper body tilted {value} away from the target; about {expected} suits a {club}.
tilt_too_much.why: Too much tilt moves the low point behind the ball and can lead to hanging back.

sway.name: Sway
sway.seen: Your hips slid {value} away from the target going back (keep it under {limit}).
sway.why: A sway puts your weight on the outside of the trail foot and makes it hard to get back to the lead side.

reverse_spine.name: Reverse spine angle
reverse_spine.seen: At the top your upper body leaned {value} toward the target.
reverse_spine.why: Leaning toward the target at the top is the leading swing cause of lower back pain, and it usually leads to hanging back.

reverse_pivot.name: Head moving toward the target
reverse_pivot.seen: Your head moved {value} toward the target going back.
reverse_pivot.why: Moving toward the target in the backswing (a reverse pivot) usually leads to falling back on the way down.

head_sway_back.name: Big head sway going back
head_sway_back.seen: Your head moved {value} away from the target going back.
head_sway_back.why: Some movement is fine; a lot makes it hard to get back to the ball consistently.

hanging_back.name: Hanging back
hanging_back.seen: Your hips were {value} toward the target at impact (aim for at least {limit}).
hanging_back.why: Not shifting onto the lead side costs speed, and fat shots are the common miss.

slide.name: Slide toward the target
slide.seen: Your hips slid {value} toward the target by impact (above {limit} is a slide).
slide.why: Sliding instead of turning makes timing hard and often leaves the club face open.

level_shoulders.name: Level shoulders at impact
level_shoulders.seen: Your shoulders were tilted only {value} at impact (good players show 30–40°).
level_shoulders.why: Level shoulders at impact are typical of an arms-dominated swing.

lunge.name: Getting ahead of the ball
lunge.seen: Your head moved {value} toward the target by impact.
lunge.why: Lunging toward the target steepens the swing and moves the low point too far forward.

hanging_back_finish.name: Finish not over the lead side
hanging_back_finish.seen: At the finish your hips were only {value} of the way across to your lead foot.
hanging_back_finish.why: Finishing on the back foot means the weight shift didn't happen.

tempo_quick_back.name: Quick backswing
tempo_quick_back.seen: Your backswing took {value} of your downswing time; good players are close to 3:1.
tempo_quick_back.why: A rushed backswing often leads to a rushed transition and the arms taking over.

tempo_slow_back.name: Long, slow backswing
tempo_slow_back.seen: Your backswing took {value} of your downswing time; good players are close to 3:1.
tempo_slow_back.why: A very slow backswing can lose rhythm and lead to a sudden hit from the top.

chip_head.name: Head moving in the chip
chip_head.seen: Your head moved {value} during the stroke.
chip_head.why: If the head moves down and back, the club hits the ground before the ball.

chip_body.name: Too much lower-body movement in the chip
chip_body.seen: Your hips moved {value} during the stroke.
chip_body.why: A quiet lower body keeps the low point consistent on short shots.

short_tempo_quick.name: Short, quick backstroke
short_tempo_quick.seen: Your backswing took {value} of your forward stroke time; about 2:1 is the reference.
short_tempo_quick.why: A short backstroke usually means a jab through the ball and poor distance control.

short_tempo_slow.name: Slow backstroke, quick through
short_tempo_slow.seen: Your backswing took {value} of your forward stroke time; about 2:1 is the reference.
short_tempo_slow.why: A long, slow backstroke often ends in deceleration or a hit.

chip_decel.name: Short follow-through
chip_decel.seen: Your follow-through was {value} of your backswing length.
chip_decel.why: Stopping at the ball means decelerating, which causes chunks and fluffs.

putt_head.name: Head moving in the putt
putt_head.seen: Your head moved {value} during the stroke.
putt_head.why: Head and body movement changes the path and where you strike the face.

putt_body.name: Body moving in the putt
putt_body.seen: Your hips moved {value} during the stroke.
putt_body.why: Only the shoulders and arms should move in a putt.

putt_decel.name: Short through-stroke
putt_decel.seen: Your through-stroke was {value} of your backstroke.
putt_decel.why: A short through-stroke usually means decelerating, which hurts distance control.

putt_long_through.name: Long through-stroke
putt_long_through.seen: Your through-stroke was {value} of your backstroke.
putt_long_through.why: A short backstroke with a long push through makes distance hard to control.

hip_hinge.name: Hip hinge with a club along your spine
steps: Hold a club along your back so it touches your head, upper back and tailbone.
Bend forward from the hips until the club stays in contact at all three points.
Add a slight knee flex, let your arms hang, then take your grip.

athletic_stance.name: Athletic stance check
steps: Stand tall, then flex your knees as if about to catch a ball.
Keep your knees roughly over the balls of your feet, not past your toes.
Hinge from the hips from there.

arm_hang.name: Let the arms hang
steps: Take your posture without a club and let your arms hang straight down.
Clap your hands together where they fall and take the grip there.
Your hands should be roughly under your shoulders.

wall_drill.name: Wall drill
steps: Set up with your backside lightly touching a wall, no club.
Make slow swings and keep your backside on the wall all the way to impact.
Do 20 slow swings; add a club once it feels natural.

chair_drill.name: Chair drill
steps: Put the back of a chair against your backside at address.
Swing slowly, feeling your trail glute push into the chair going back and your lead glute stay on it coming down.
If you lose contact before impact, you're moving toward the ball.

club_across_shoulders.name: Club across the shoulders
steps: Hold a club across your chest at the shoulders and take your posture.
Turn to the top of your backswing.
The club should point at the ground beyond the ball, not at the horizon.

headcover_gate.name: Headcover outside the ball
steps: Place a headcover about 15–20 cm behind the ball, just outside the target line.
Make swings that miss the headcover on the way down.
Start with half swings.

hands_to_bicep.name: Hands down to the trail bicep
steps: Swing to the top and pause.
Start down by letting your hands drop so they line up with your trail bicep, not out toward the ball.
Rehearse 10 times, then hit balls with the same feel.

hold_finish.name: Hold your finish
steps: After each shot hold your finish for a count of three.
Check: weight on the lead foot, trail heel up, belt buckle facing the target.
If you wobble or step back, slow the swing down.

step_through.name: Step-through drill
steps: Make a normal backswing.
As you swing through, let your trail foot step forward toward the target.
This only works if your weight has moved onto your lead side.

club_drop_stance.name: Club-drop stance check
steps: Take your stance and hold a club against the outside of each shoulder in turn.
Let it hang down: for a mid-iron it should touch the middle of each foot.
Go slightly wider for woods and slightly narrower for wedges.

hip_bump_setup.name: Hip bump at setup
steps: Put an alignment stick on the ground in line with the ball.
At address, bump your hips slightly toward the target so your nose sits behind the stick.
Keep the nose behind the stick as you swing back.

trail_hip_stick.name: Stick outside the trail hip
steps: Push an alignment stick into the ground about 5 cm outside your trail hip.
Make backswings without bumping it: turn the hip back, don't slide it out.
Start with half swings.

feet_together.name: Feet-together swings
steps: Hit half and three-quarter shots with your feet almost touching.
You can only stay balanced by turning, not sliding.

nose_behind_stick.name: Nose behind the stick
steps: Lay an alignment stick on the ground in line with the ball.
Keep your nose on the trail side of the stick through the backswing and into impact.

cross_arms_pivot.name: Cross-arms pivot
steps: Without a club, cross your arms over your chest and take your posture.
Turn back, feeling your weight go into your trail leg.
Turn through, getting your pressure onto your lead foot and your chest to the target.

impact_tilt.name: Impact tilt rehearsal
steps: Move slowly into an impact position: belt buckle over your front foot, head over the middle of your stance.
Feel your trail shoulder lower than your lead shoulder.
Hold for three seconds, repeat five times, then hit half shots.

tempo_count.name: Tempo count
steps: Count "one, two, three" going back and "one" coming down to impact.
Or use a tempo metronome at 24/8 or 27/9.
Keep the ratio the same at any speed.

chip_setup.name: Chip setup and quiet head
steps: Narrow stance, ball in the middle, about two-thirds of your weight on the lead foot.
Hands slightly ahead of the ball.
Keep your head and chest from dropping back as you swing through.

short_tempo.name: Short-game 2:1 count
steps: Count "one, two" back and "one" through.
Change the length of the stroke, not the speed, to change distance.

chip_three_stroke.name: Three-stroke continuous chip
steps: Set up with your weight forward.
Swing back and through three times without stopping, brushing the grass each time.
Then hit a ball with the same through-motion.

listen_dont_look.name: Listen, don't look
steps: On short putts keep your eyes on the spot where the ball was until you hear it drop.
Rock your shoulders; keep your hips and head still.

putt_matching.name: Matched stroke lengths
steps: Put two tees an equal distance behind and ahead of the ball.
Swing the putter from one tee to the other at the same pace.

gate_drill.name: Gate drill
steps: Place two tees just wider than the ball about a metre ahead on your line.
Roll putts through the gate.

bodyNote: If drills don't change this, a coach or a TPI-certified professional can check whether mobility is the limit. If anything hurts, stop.
